lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: A quiet camp can still reveal a lot - and this one has a bright, expensive centerpiece. Gavin McKenna opened training camp on John Tavares' wing with William Nylander, a lineup look that says the Leafs want skill, speed and a little shelter around the rookie while the building adjusts to a new season. Toronto's record is finished at 2025-26's end, and the only number that matters now is what comes next: an opening-night roster. Chris Tanev's return matters here too; a healthy season from him would steady a blue line that still needs old-man composure and clean exits. The classic centre-ice logo is a tidy nod to history, but the real story is whether this club finally builds something sturdier around its young talent. Watch camp battles, especially McKenna's deployment and Tanev's workload, because that will tell the truth.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: Momentum has slipped into a thin, uncomfortable autumn. The Blue Jays are staring at an offseason that demands clarity, not comfort - and the latest jolt is Dylan Cease's fading fastball, with his velocity now a real concern. Toronto's season is over, and the final 76-77 mark leaves the front office with no escape hatch and no room for wishful thinking. Cease remains the headline arm, but if his heater is losing life, every roster conversation gets sharper, from the rotation to the bullpen to the health reports that still crowd the ledger. The club also has to sort through the end-of-season minor league churn and decide which arms are ready to matter next spring. What to watch now is whether Toronto answers the pitching question with patience or action before camp opens.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: Quiet usually means the calendar has gone soft, but in Toronto it's the opposite: the offseason is where the next punch gets loaded. The Raptors and Kawhi Leonard are closing in on a contract extension - the kind of move that tells you the franchise has chosen its veteran pivot and intends to live with the consequences. Toronto's own bookkeeping says the season is over, which leaves the focus squarely on September's chessboard: the coaching staff has been reshuffled, Darko Rajaković has his bench, and the room is being built around Leonard's fit. He is the story now, not as a highlight machine, but as a risk-reward ledger in a city that remembers 2019. Training camp opens in the coming weeks, and that's when the real answers start.

the_latest.dek: Kawhi Leonard's return puts Toronto under a microscope, because the fit will shape both the team's ceiling and the offseason's direction. His impact on spacing, availability and defensive balance will determine whether the move becomes a short-term boost or a franchise reset.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The calendar says offseason, but the microscope is already back on the Commanders' passing game - because that's where the noise lives, and where the answers have to come from. Jayden Daniels is being asked not to force-feed Terry McLaurin, a delicate line for any young quarterback and a dangerous one if Washington lets its best receiver drift to the margins. McLaurin's 14-yard opener was a shrug, not a statement, and that cannot become the habit. Washington is 0-1, but the record matters less now than the construction of the thing: Daniels, McLaurin, and a receiver room that has to stretch the field, not just decorate it. Dorance Armstrong's return to Dallas adds bite up front. What to watch next: whether McLaurin becomes the engine again, or merely a name on the depth chart.

the_latest.headline: Terry McLaurin can share the load but Commanders cannot let him disappear
the_latest.dek: Washington's rebuilt receiver group is supposed to ease the burden on Terry McLaurin, but the offense still needs him to remain a clear focal point. If he drifts into the background, the Commanders risk turning added depth into a much smaller threat on game day.

article.title: Friday's Skate
paragraphs: The Leafs opened the morning with a nod to their past, dropping a classic logo at centre ice as attention starts shifting toward what Chris Tanev can bring in 2026-27. For the Blue Jays, the focus is less nostalgic and more urgent, with playoff odds being weighed after the series loss to Detroit and minor league notes wrapping up the season.

The Raptors have the most intriguing offseason item, with reports saying Kawhi Leonard and the team are closing in on a contract extension, while new fit questions are already circulating. In Washington, the Commanders turn to Week 2 against Dallas, with Terry McLaurin again central to the passing game and the load he has to carry.
